extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and narrative studies / humanities scholars interested in LLM-driven story generation and understanding
extracted.subtask_description: A survey of how narrative theories and narratology are applied to LLM-based NLP systems for automatic story generation and understanding, categorising tasks, datasets, narrative-theoretical framings, and evaluation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence (plot consistency, logical relationships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures whether a system can depict complex logical relationships between story events, characters, and actions — i.e., whether generated narratives maintain plot consistency and believability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper notes early rule-based methods struggled with coherence; LLMs outperform earlier models in maintaining plot consistency and generating longer, coherent narratives. Evaluation should target causal links between events, consistency of character actions over time, and believability of event sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Linguistic fluency of produced text (naturalness, grammaticality, readability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMs are credited with improved fluency relative to prior symbolic/neural approaches. Fluency is an orthogonal but necessary criterion alongside higher-level narrative attributes and is typically measured via human ratings or automatic language-model-based metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which generated stories display novelty, inventiveness, and interesting narrative choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey cites narrative-theory integration as a way to enhance creativity. Evaluation may include human judgments of originality, diversity of plot/structure, and structural diversity metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional engagement / Empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity of a narrative to evoke emotion, provoke empathy, and engage readers (e.g., empathy toward characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites work (Shen et al., Harel-Canada et al.) using scales such as the Psychological Depth Scale and crowdsourced empathy evaluations. Practical evaluation involves correlating annotated narrative features (characterisation, internal perspective) with human empathy ratings and using both human raters and model-based judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with human narrative conventions / believability
rubrics_metrics.description: How well outputs align with established narrative conventions and reader expectations (e.g., beginning–middle–end structures, archetypal roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrating narratology is argued to improve alignment. Assess with expert annotations referencing narratological constructs (e.g., Propp, Freytag) and with human judgments of believability and structural appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controllability (of generated content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which a system allows targeted control over narrative attributes (plot, character behaviour, style, register).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey notes LLMs improve controllability; evaluation should test targeted prompting/fine-tuning interventions and measure fidelity of output to constraints (e.g., enforced plot points, POV, timeline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to identify thematic patterns and contextual/historical links
rubrics_metrics.description: Model capability to detect subtle thematic patterns and connect narratives to broader cultural or historical contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMs reportedly surpass earlier methods here. Evaluation examples include theme classification, linking to myths/history, and qualitative analyses showing thematic extraction across corpora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative level: Fabula (story/histoire) evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of systems operating at the fabula (chronological sequence of events) level: correctness/completeness of event sequences, event ordering, and story-world facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks include extracting or constructing chronological event sequences and social networks from narratives. Metrics should measure chronological correctness, event coverage, causal chain plausibility, and social-network fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative level: Discourse (text/presentation) evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of how the story is presented (voice, focalisation, temporal arrangement, style) — i.e., discourse-level qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes measuring tense/mood/voice, prompt style/register effects, narrative pacing and rhetorical choices. Operationalisation examples: annotating discourse features and testing LLM annotation and generation conditioned on discourse constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative level: Narration evaluation (narrator, narratee, perspective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of narratorial properties: narrator position (extradiegetic/intradiegetic), homodiegetic/heterodiegetic status, narratee presence, and narrator reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work such as Brei et al. evaluates unreliable narrators. Evaluation can include classification of narrator type, detection of reliability cues, and generation conditioned on narrator perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrativity as a scalar quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measuring the degree to which a text exhibits narrative qualities (temporal progression, causal linkage, agents and events) on a continuous scale instead of binary classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Piper & Bagga annotate passages with narrativity scores; evaluation frameworks should aggregate passage-level features to produce scalar narrativity values and compare model vs human ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event causality / causal reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Model ability to detect, represent, and reason about causal relations between events in narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey emphasises event causality as key to story understanding (Sun et al.). Tests include causal inference tasks, causal graph construction, and evaluating causal chain validity in generation and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character role identification and character modelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of character roles (protagonist, antagonist, hero, villain, victim) and representation of character similarity or distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Zhou et al. use GPT-4 to label roles in news; Yang & Anderson provide a character similarity benchmark. Evaluation includes classification accuracy for role labels and similarity rankings compared to gold annotations or human judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turning point / reportable event identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Detecting narrative turning points or reportable events that change the story state (e.g., key events, climaxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks include labeling turning points (Ouyang & McKeown; Tian et al.). Evaluate detection precision/recall against annotated turning points and measure impact on downstream summarisation or plot-tracking tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative feature labeling (tense, mood, voice, anachrony, POV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotating formal discourse features such as tense, mood, voice, pastness, anachrony, and point-of-view to operationalise narratological frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Piper & Bagga map Genette’s discourse theory to measurable features embedded in prompts and validated by human annotators. Use inter-annotator agreement, annotation accuracy, and downstream utility as evaluation signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator reliability detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to detect unreliable narrators and different types of unreliability in narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brei et al. evaluate LLMs on detecting unreliable narrators. Use labeled datasets of reliable vs unreliable narration and error analyses explaining why models succeed/fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological depth (reader response dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurements of psychological/affective complexity in stories: emotion provocation, authenticity, engagement, narrative complexity, and identification with characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harel-Canada et al. employ the Psychological Depth Scale. Evaluation can mix expert scales, crowd judgments, and correlations with linguistic cues tied to cognitive narratology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral identification / moral framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracting or classifying morals, frames, or ideological stances within narratives (e.g., news framing, fairy-tale morals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zhou et al. and others examine morals and frames in news and fairytales. Evaluation involves classification/annotation of moral frames and measuring cross-source patterns and cultural differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual / cultural framing and transgeneric analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing how narratives reflect or construct cultural identities, values, and cross-genre/transmodal properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual narratology work examines group-level values in news/fairytales and cross-cultural patterns. Evaluation includes cross-source comparisons, cultural-sensitivity metrics, and domain-aware annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability and suitability for large-scale, theory-driven analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether methods/datasets enable large-scale annotation and distant-reading style analysis grounded in narrative theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey highlights LLMs' low-cost, practical potential for large-scale testing and distant reading. Evaluation includes throughput, annotation quality at scale, and reproducibility across large corpora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking and evaluation frameworks (datasets, baselines, metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for standardised datasets, baselines, and metrics tailored to narrative tasks to enable fair model comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey points out the absence of unified narrative benchmarks; recommends defining theory-based metrics for individual narrative attributes rather than a single generalised 'narrative quality' benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset diversity and provenance (fiction, non-fiction, social media, news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the types of textual sources used for narrative tasks and how domain affects annotation and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper documents use of novels, short stories, news, social media, clinical settings, multilingual corpora; evaluation must account for domain-specific narrativity, genre conventions, and domain biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation schemes and segmentation (clause-level event/subjective/contextual labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of annotation schemes for narrative constituents (e.g., clause-level event vs subjective vs contextual labels) and segmentation into narrative units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Troiano & Vossen's CLAUSE-ATLAS and other works provide clause-level schemes. Evaluate via inter-annotator agreement, LLM annotation accuracy, and downstream task performance when using these annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling hallucinations and confabulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of model hallucinations: distinguishing harmful/unreliable hallucinations from potentially useful confabulations for creative/narrative tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sui et al. argue confabulation can have surprising value. Evaluation should distinguish factual correctness requirements from creative acceptability, and include analyses of when hallucination aids creativity vs when it undermines trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation protocols and LLM-as-judge alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Using human raters, crowdsourced judgments, and LLMs-as-evaluators to assess narrative attributes and measuring alignment between these evaluators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey cites discrepancies between crowd worker and expert ratings. Protocols should include expert and crowd studies, calibration of LLM-judges, and analysis of systematic differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory-of-mind (ToM) and social reasoning via narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing models' ability to reason about characters' beliefs, intentions, and mental states via narrative tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zhou et al. 2025 and other work use narratives to probe ToM. Evaluation tasks include QA about characters' beliefs, predicting behaviour, and measuring contextual understanding of mental states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal meaning and processing (temporal relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model competence at representing and reasoning about temporal relations and temporal meaning in narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De Langis et al. and Yang et al. highlight persistent struggles with temporal and causal reasoning. Evaluate via temporally-focused benchmarks, temporal ordering tasks, and narrative timeline reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form / book-length story evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics and evaluation protocols specialized for book-length or long-form narratives (coherence over long contexts, character arcs across many pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yang & Jin (2025) study what matters in evaluating book-length stories. Evaluation should consider long-range coherence, sustained character development, pacing, and structural arcs, using specialised datasets and human reviewer protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual and multi-domain narrative extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to extract narrative components across languages and domains, and to support multilingual benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites datasets like PolyNarrative and SemEval tasks; evaluation includes multilingual extraction accuracy, cross-lingual consistency, and domain transfer robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative embeddings and representation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of vector/structured representations capturing narrative semantics for downstream tasks (retrieval, clustering, similarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatzel & Biemann (2024a) create narrative embeddings. Evaluation includes intrinsic metrics (cluster purity, nearest-neighbour quality) and extrinsic utility in tasks like character similarity, plot retrieval, and narrative classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment dynamics and character-relationship tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracking sentiment variance and evolving relationships between characters across a narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works cited track sentiment variance and relationship evolution across novels; evaluation uses temporal relationship annotations, change-point detection, and correlation with plot events.
